questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How virtual assistants change the way we use technology
How to fix a broken smartphone
Why people are losing their watches
The best smart speakers and phones to buy for your home
questions.why: They discuss virtual assistants and how they are changing the way we interact with technology.

questions.q: Why did Rob ask Dan the time at the start?
options: His watch was broken
He wanted to make a joke
He was trying to introduce the topic
He was late for a meeting
questions.why: Rob says 'I was trying to introduce today's topic which is all about virtual assistants'.

questions.q: According to Tom Hewitson, how have we mostly thought of computers until now?
options: As friends
As tools, like an advanced calculator
As dangerous machines
As toys
questions.why: He says we've thought of them largely as tools, 'just an advanced version of a calculator'.

questions.q: How does Hewitson say virtual assistants are changing computers?
options: They are making them cheaper
They are making them smaller, so they fit in our pockets and homes
They are making them slower
They are making them active participants that guide us
questions.why: He says they are becoming 'an active participant in the interaction and in guiding you'.

questions.q: What does Rob joke his virtual assistant would tell him?
options: He spends too much time in fast food restaurants
He talks too much
He spends too much time in the gym
He needs a new watch
questions.why: Rob says 'Mine would be telling me I spend too much time in the gym!'

questions.q: According to Hewitson, what won't we need to do when talking to machines?
options: Speak clearly
Make small talk so the machine likes us
Ask short, direct questions without any extra words
Use our own language
questions.why: He says 'you don't need to make the machine like you' or make random chit-chat.

questions.q: How does Hewitson think our language with machines will be?
options: More polite than with people
Exactly the same as with people
Full of jokes
More direct and less polite
questions.why: He says it can be 'much more brusque and to the point'.

questions.q: Why does Dan mention that the IBM Shoebox recognised 16 words?
options: To joke that Rob knows about as many words
To show computers were very clever then
To explain how bots learn
To say it was better than modern assistants
questions.why: Dan says 'That's nearly as many as you!' and Rob replies 'Cheeky!'
